thread:
ashwin: thinking about the quota_profile -> canonical_quota_id migration. sketching a plan; want feedback on safety + console UX impact.

maria: +1. main concern is dashboards and per-route quotas — queries that JOIN on quota_profile name will break if we start using an opaque id. need read-adapter approach.

jonathan: agreed. can we add a read shim column `quota_profile_aliases` while we roll? that preserves human-readable lookups in console.

ashwin: that's the idea. proposal: add canonical_quota_id (bigint), keep quota_profile_name (text) until dual-write + backfill done. API will accept name or id for a transition period.

hee-jin: timeline? backfill is expensive on telemetry tables. we should do incremental windowed backfills and dual-write for 2 weeks. also add a safe-mapping table for name -> id (immutable mapping).

kyle: sketch of SQL for the schema change:
```sql
ALTER TABLE console.quotas ADD COLUMN canonical_quota_id bigint DEFAULT NULL;
-- create mapping table
CREATE TABLE console.quota_aliases (canonical_quota_id bigint PRIMARY KEY, quota_profile_name text NOT NULL);
```
Backfill job will populate canonical_quota_id by joining on alias table.

maria: for telemetry/analytics store (huge) we should not modify the wide events table immediately. instead: dualwrite from ingestion, and write a lightweight materialized lookup table that analytics queries can JOIN to avoid rewriting big tables. Backfill only for routes with >X events.

jonathan: +1 — canary on a single tenant with high activity. also add a query-time fallback resolver in the console that does a lookup if canonical_quota_id is null. This keeps dashboards working.

ashwin: UX: in Console settings add a toggle "Prefer canonical quota id" with per-tenant opt-in. Default off until we finish backfills. We'll surface which dashboards rely on name-based joins so owners can migrate.

hee-jin: telemetry: emit events for migration stages so we can monitor errors and coverage. e.g. `quota_migration_dualwrite_enabled`, `quota_backfill_pct`, `quota_read_adapter_fallbacks` as counters.

telemetry-bot: metric created: quota_migration_dualwrite_enabled (gauge)

kyle: operational concerns: backfill windows should be rate-limited, idempotent, and resumable. propose windowed backfill by event_time with 1h windows and 5 concurrent workers; throttle metrics at 2000 rows/s to avoid saturating ingestion.

maria: queries to update analytics:
```sql
-- idempotent upsert per window
INSERT INTO console.quota_backfill_progress (window_start, window_end, status) VALUES (...)
ON CONFLICT (window_start) DO NOTHING;
UPDATE analytics.events e SET canonical_quota_id = a.canonical_quota_id
FROM console.quota_aliases a
WHERE e.quota_profile_name = a.quota_profile_name
  AND e.event_time >= :window_start AND e.event_time < :window_end;
```

jonathan: We also need a canary dashboard that compares token cost and latency for queries joining on name vs joining on id. If id-based plans are faster we can accelerate migration.

ashwin: rollout gating checklist:
- dual-write ingestion enabled & verified for 48h
- small tenant canary backfill completed & console toggle tested
- telemetry coverage >= 95% for canonical_quota_id present on ingested events
- run cost/latency compare dashboard for 1 day
- start progressive backfill for 10% tenants, monitor errors
- full backfill pass for high-volume tenants only, leave low-volume for on-read resolver

maria: fallback behavior in Console UI: if canonical_quota_id missing show a subtle warning and a resolver link that runs a lookup (async) to populate id for that route. avoids 500s.

hee-jin: failure modes: missing alias mapping -> create an operator flow where owners can map unknown names to canonical ids; any unmapped entries go to a dead-letter table for manual review.

kyle: deployment plan: DB migrations first (add columns + alias table + backfill_progress table), deploy ingestion dualwrite, enable feature flag, start backfill workers, enable console toggle for canary tenant.

deploy-bot: started backfill worker job 37498 for tenant `acme-corp` window 2025-08-01T00:00:00Z -> 2025-08-01T01:00:00Z

jonathan: one more: permissioning. ensure alias table writes are limited to platform jobs / ops users. don't expose writes to regular API.

ashwin: +1. also add an admin endpoint to re-run missed windows and to surface backfill progress to Console's rollout UX.

maria: sounds like a plan. I'll draft the PRs and the Console toggle UI copy. can we decide on the opt-in period length? proposing 2 weeks opt-in after dual-write verified, then start auto-migration for high-volume tenants with owner notif.

ashwin: 2 weeks sounds reasonable. thanks all — will create tracking task and link PRs.

jonathan: if folks want, I'll assemble the canary dashboards and alerting queries.

ashwin: please do. ping here when ready.
